compiled_state.description:
## This is a chosen trade, not a regression to re-investigate

Change 2684 (bug `ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` / `9313-1fac-9f32-4b07`) lowers `DOCKER_DU_TIMEOUT`
from 120 s to 60 s and routes it through the whole-probe budget. A direct and **deliberate**
consequence is that under I/O load the filesystem walk will not finish, so
`docker_storage_bytes`, `docker_storage_used_percent` and `docker_unaccounted_bytes` will
publish **nothing** for those intervals.

This ticket exists so that is a recorded decision rather than a mystery. Somebody seeing
`docker_storage_bytes` gaps next month should find this ticket, not start a fresh investigation
— which is exactly the failure mode `9313` itself was: a day spent on "sparse publishing"
because a truncated run and an absent value were indistinguishable.

**Distinguishing signal:** a gap here with `docker_du_seconds` at or near 60 and `probe_ok` = 1
is THIS, working as designed — the walk was attempted, bounded, and did not finish, and the rest
of the probe completed normally. A gap with `probe_ok` absent or `probe_truncated` = 1 is a
different problem and belongs to `9313`'s revert conditions.

## The measurement — the Docker root cannot be walked in this budget

On the production Gerrit host, 2026-09-05, load average 3.45 (the ordinary condition, not a
pathological one):

    95.01s  rc=124  timeout 95  du -x --block-size=1 --max-depth=1 /var/lib/docker
    95.01s  rc=124  timeout 95  du -x --block-size=1 --max-depth=1 /var/lib/docker
   125.03s  rc=124  timeout 125 du -sx --block-size=1 /var/lib/docker
   125.04s  rc=124  timeout 125 du -sx --block-size=1 /var/lib/docker/overlay2

**A single walk did not complete at 95 s, and did not complete at 125 s.** Twice each. So this
is not "the old code walked twice, halve it and it fits" — the tree is simply larger than the
budget under load. ~1.88M files, and `install-observability.sh` runs the unit at
`IOSchedulingClass=idle` and `Nice=10`, so the walk is starved by design on a box whose job is
serving Gerrit and which has documented IOPS-saturation history
(`smudgeless-friendless-longspur`).

**That is a capacity finding, not a defect.** `9313` is the defect (uncomposed ceilings, and a
probe SIGTERM-ed mid-run); this is the physics underneath it.

## Why 60 s is nevertheless the right bound

The reading is **bimodal**, not slow-and-variable. When the cache is warm the walk completes in
well under a minute — journald breadcrumbs at 17:48, 17:58, 18:03, 18:09 and 18:42 on
2026-09-05 all carry a `docker /var/lib/docker bytes=` value. Under load it does not complete
at any bound tried.

Given two modes and nothing in between, a 120 s attempt that fails costs a further minute of a
240 s budget over a 60 s attempt that fails, and returns the same nothing. 60 s captures the
fast mode and fails fast in the stalled one. Raising it back would not recover the metric; it
would only re-create `9313`.

## What is lost

- `docker_unaccounted_bytes` — the highest-value metric here, and the one the 2026-09-02
  incident exists to justify: overlay2 measured from the FILESYSTEM minus what
  `docker system df` accounts for, i.e. the bytes no `docker prune` can reach. It needs the
  filesystem half, so it is silent whenever the walk is.
- `docker_storage_bytes` / `docker_storage_used_percent` — the cap-in-force readings.
- Their alarms are `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, so **these gaps will page.** That is the
  correct behaviour for a dead publisher and the wrong behaviour for a bounded, deliberate
  non-measurement, and reconciling the two is part of this ticket's work rather than something
  to paper over by weakening the alarms.

## Options, none yet chosen — this needs measurement, not a preference

1. **Walk less.** `overlay2/*/diff` is the bulk. A `--max-depth=2` census over `overlay2` alone,
   or sampling layer directories, trades exactness for completion. Needs measuring: it may not
   be meaningfully cheaper, since the cost is the stat walk, not the aggregation.
2. **A cheaper estimator.** XFS/ext4 project quotas or `df` on a dedicated Docker volume give an
   O(1) reading. ADR 0112 already moved gate scratch to its own volume for a related reason;
   giving `/var/lib/docker` its own filesystem would make `docker_storage_bytes` a `df` read.
   Probably the real answer, and the largest change.
3. **Move the census out of band.** A separate low-frequency unit with a long timeout writes a
   cache the probe reads, publishing `docker_census_age_seconds` so staleness is explicit. Keeps
   the metric at reduced freshness instead of losing it.
4. **Accept that it is unobtainable at this tree size** and retire the filesystem half, saying
   so — which would also retire `docker_unaccounted_bytes`. The honest option, and the one to
   beat.

Whichever is chosen, the alarm treatment for a deliberate non-measurement must be settled with
it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The chosen option is measured against the alternatives on the production host, not
      selected on plausibility — including the negative case, that walking less is not cheaper.
- [ ] `docker_unaccounted_bytes` is either restored to continuous publication, or explicitly
      retired with the incident rationale addressed.
- [ ] The alarms stop paging for a bounded non-measurement while still paging for a dead
      publisher — the two are distinguishable via `probe_ok` / `docker_du_seconds` as of 2684.
- [ ] `docker_du_seconds` is used as the before/after evidence.
- [ ] Portability: host shell + systemd + local validation; no dependence on a single CI provider.

## Provenance

Measured 2026-09-05 while fixing `9313`. The 95 s and 125 s negative results are what stopped a
"halve the walk" fix from shipping: removing the second traversal makes the probe survive, and
does NOT make the reading obtainable. Recording the trade here so the degradation is a decision
with evidence attached rather than an undocumented behaviour change.
compiled_state.title: docker_storage_bytes and docker_unaccounted_bytes will go intermittently blind under load — an ACCEPTED, measured degradation from bug 9313, because the Docker root cannot be walked inside the probe's budget
